Script 1: Nam’s hobby (collecting stamps)

Mai: Hi Nam, do you have any hobbies?
Nam: Yes, I really enjoy collecting stamps. I started when I was ten.
Mai: Wow! How many stamps do you have now?
Nam: More than 200. I keep them in an album.
Mai: That’s amazing. Do you spend much time on it?
Nam: Of course. I usually look for new stamps at the weekend. Sometimes I swap stamps with my friends.
Mai: Sounds fun!
Nam: Yes, it helps me relax after school, and I also learn about different countries.

Script 2: Community service at orphanage
Last Sunday, my class joined a community service activity at a local orphanage. We brought some old clothes, toys, and books for the children. Some of my classmates played games with them, while others taught the children how to draw and sing. We also cleaned the rooms and the yard. The children were very happy and smiled a lot. At the end of the day, we felt tired but also proud, because we knew we had done something meaningful for the community.

sections.title: III. Read the following passage and answer the questions. (1.25 points)
sections.introHtml: Living a healthy life is very important for teenagers. A good diet with vegetables, fruit, fish, and rice gives the body energy and vitamins. Drinking enough water also keeps us healthy. Doctors suggest about eight glasses a day. Doing exercise is another key to staying fit. Activities such as jogging, cycling, or playing football make the body stronger and the mind happier. Sleep is also necessary. Teenagers should sleep at least seven hours each night. Without enough sleep, students feel tired and cannot study well. In short, healthy eating, regular exercise, enough water, and good sleep help teenagers stay strong and do better at school.

2. Content: (0.4 point): a provision of main ideas and details as appropriate to the main idea.
